editorial.thesis: A hospitality city of about 12,000. Its retail is thin on pharmacy & health retail and apparel, footwear & jewellery — and 0% of residents live in zones with under 60% of the city's average retail depth.
takeaways: Branded retail is about 0% of Mumbai's. 0.0 chain outlets per lakh residents against 23.76 in Mumbai; 0 of the 51 national brands we track are present.

The mapped economy leans to hotels & stays. Shares of all mapped places: hotels & stays 50.0% (Mumbai 4.2%). Raw counts would mislead because Mumbai is mapped more completely (70,423 places against 226), so we compare mix, not counts.

numbers.title: The city in eight numbers
numbers.deck: A 5 km circle around the centre, processed with the same rules as Mumbai, so every comparison is like for like. Where raw counts would mislead — because a bigger city is mapped more completely — we compare shares and mix instead.

map.title: Where people live, where shops are
map.deck: Switch layers. The amber “gap” layer is the one to study: it marks places with many residents but little retail around them. Hover any hexagon (about 0.1 km²) for its numbers; click a zone on the right to isolate it.

captions.residents: Where people live. Matheran is the only mapped zone, with about 5,000 residents. Modelled residents per square kilometre.
captions.supply: Where the shops are. The busiest tenth of cells hold 52% of all commercial places, and Matheran alone lists 108.
captions.chains: Where the brands are. Matheran holds 0 of the 0 tracked chain outlets.
captions.education: Where the campuses are. Matheran has 1 education places and 0 coaching centres.
captions.gap: The gap. Amber: many residents nearby, little retail. Blue: far more retail than local residents explain — the commercial cores that draw people in. There is no large amber area. The blue cores include Matheran.

zones.title: Zone by zone, by PIN code
zones.deck: Each zone is a postal-code area. Residents are modelled counts; places are mapped businesses and services. “Retail depth” is places per 10,000 residents — the tick marks the city average. Click a row to see it on the map.

mix.title: What the retail layer is made of
mix.deck: Raw counts per resident would favour whichever city is mapped more completely (70,423 places in Mumbai against 226 here). So this compares each category's share of all mapped places. 100 means the same share as Mumbai; below 100 is thinner, above is stronger.
mix.note: Against Mumbai, Matheran's mapped places over-index on hotels & stays (50.0% vs 4.2%).

chains.title: Who is mapped here, and who is not
chains.deck: 0 outlets of 0 tracked national brands within 5 km — 0.0 per lakh residents against Mumbai's 23.76 (1266 outlets of 44 brands). Filled names have at least one mapped outlet (count shown); dashed names have none.
chains.note: Read dashed names as leads, not verdicts. “No mapped outlet” can mean a brand trades under a different listed name, or has opened since the map was updated. The widest gaps against Mumbai are Café Coffee Day (0 vs 169); Domino's (0 vs 115); Subway (0 vs 81). Premium reports check every lead against live listings.

formats.title: Which formats have room
formats.deck: 9 formats, thinnest first. The index is the format's share of all mapped places relative to Mumbai's, so low means thin by Mumbai's standard. “Where to look” ranks zones with at least 40,000 residents by residents per mapped outlet — a first-pass screen for where one more outlet would face the least local competition.

people.title: Who the customers are
people.deck: Age mix inside the 5 km circle, from Meta's age rasters (modelled, not a census).
people.note: Matheran's age mix against Mumbai: children (0–14) 23.5% vs 19.9%, 15–24 18.7% vs 19.7%, working age 48.6% vs 52.0%, 60+ 9.2% vs 8.4%. Under-25s are 42% of residents.

zones.410102: A commercial core: 108 mapped places and 0 chain outlets (0% of the city's tracked chains) for about 5,000 residents. A destination zone, so much of its footfall likely lives elsewhere.

restaurants.read: Restaurants & fast food are 5.3% of mapped places against 7.0% in Mumbai — below its share.
restaurants.watch: Independent eateries are numerous and unevenly mapped. Treat the index as a screen and confirm competitor density street by street.

cafes.read: Cafés, tea & coffee are 0.4% of mapped places against 2.7% in Mumbai — below its share.
cafes.watch: Chai stalls and independent cafés are under-mapped. A café concept here competes on price and habit as much as on novelty.

desserts.read: Desserts, sweets & ice cream are 0.4% of mapped places against 1.1% in Mumbai — below its share. No mapped outlet in either city: Cream Stone.
desserts.watch: Traditional sweet shops are the real benchmark and sit outside most chain lists.

grocery.read: Grocery & daily needs are 1.8% of mapped places against 1.9% in Mumbai, so the mix is level. No mapped outlet in either city: More, Vishal Mega Mart, Easyday.
grocery.watch: Neighbourhood kirana stores are the real incumbents and the least completely mapped outlets, so any gap is overstated. Test a site against local store density before acting.

pharmacy.read: Pharmacy & health retail are 0.0% of mapped places against 1.3% in Mumbai — below its share. No mapped outlet in either city: Frank Ross.
pharmacy.watch: Independent chemists are dense and lightly mapped. Hospital and clinic clusters are the natural anchors.

apparel.read: Apparel, footwear & jewellery are 0.0% of mapped places against 4.8% in Mumbai — below its share. No mapped outlet in either city: Zudio, V-Mart.
apparel.watch: Established multi-brand traders and local bazaars sit behind these numbers; new entrants compete with them as well as with chains.

banking.read: Banks & ATMs are 1.8% of mapped places against 7.8% in Mumbai — below its share.
banking.watch: This category includes insurance and agency offices, so it overstates branch banking. Use it as a signal of commercial activity, not a branch count.

coaching.read: Coaching & training are 0.4% of mapped places against 2.7% in Mumbai — below its share.
coaching.watch: Coaching demand follows the exam calendar. Formats that depend on it should be tested across the academic year.

fitness.read: Fitness & wellness are 0.4% of mapped places against 4.4% in Mumbai — below its share.
fitness.watch: Gym listings change often and are inconsistently categorised; verify before drawing conclusions.
